draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Arambol! It's a traditional fishing village up in Pernem, with a long beach that's part rocky, part sandy. Seasoned Anjuna regulars like to stay here for the quiet and only head south for parties and markets.
draft.hungryLine: Cafes and restaurants line the shore all the way from the little Sweet Water Lake beach down to Mandrem, so take your pick.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Climb the headland at the end of the beach for a lovely view and its small altars, then wander north to Keri Beach.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Stroll south along the sand towards Mandrem Beach, this stretch is known for its relative quietude.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The sea here is warmest from April to June, averaging around 29 °C.

tips.title: Come in the dry season.
tips.body: The main tourist season runs through the dry months, roughly December to April, and the sunniest days get about 10 hours of sun.

tips.title: Try paragliding.
tips.body: Paragliding is one of Arambol's main draws, along with the nearby hot water springs.

story.title: A fishing village
story.body: Arambol started as a traditional fishing village in Pernem, about 24.6 km north of Panaji. Its beach sits between Keri to the north and Mandrem to the south.

story.title: A small village
story.body: Around 5,300 people lived in Arambol in 2011. It still feels like a village, with open drains and tap water from a treated source.

story.title: Winter crowds
story.body: International visitors come mainly between November and March. Cafes have mushroomed all along the shoreline to welcome them.
